articles.title: Barnham residents vote for independence from UK to protest asylum seeker housing at RAF base
articles.description: The English village of Barnham in Suffolk held a local referendum in which 257 residents voted for independence from the United Kingdom, while 16 voted against. The move was prompted by the government's plan to house 931 asylum seekers near the village, a number that is almost twice the total population of Barnham, which stands at 584. According to Sky News, authorities have selected the former Royal Air Force base RAF Barnham for the accommodation. The residents are primarily men awaiting the processing of their asylum applications, though their specific countries of origin have not been disclosed. A final decision on opening the center has not yet been made. As the British government moves away from the costly practice of housing migrants in hotels, it is increasingly repurposing former military sites. This shift has brought the migrant crisis, previously associated mainly with London and other major urban centers, to the rural English countryside.
